title: First constraint on Born-rule violations at high-energy colliders
abstract: We obtain an experimental constraint on possible Born-rule violations at high-energy colliders. We model Born-rule violations with differential scattering cross sections $dσ/dΩ$ subject to an angular smearing by a narrow Gaussian of width $\varepsilon$ (with respect to $x=\cosθ$ for scattering angle $θ$). For large-angle Bhabha ($e^{+}e^{-} \rightarrow e^{+}e^{-}$) scattering, at a centre-of-mass energy $\sqrt{s}=29\, \mathrm{GeV}$, data from the PEP collider at SLAC allow us to set an upper bound of $\varepsilon<0.042$ at $95\%$ confidence. This corresponds to a Gaussian smearing over an angular range of twice the experimental bin width, and hence provides a physically meaningful limit on deviations from the Born rule. Future prospects for improving this limit are discussed.
summary: This paper derives an experimental constraint on potential violations of the Born rule by analyzing Bhabha scattering data from the PEP collider. The authors model deviations as an angular smearing parameter ($\epsilon$) and use statistical fitting techniques to set an upper bound of $\epsilon < 0.042$. This provides a rigorous, model-independent test of quantum mechanics at high energies.
main_problem: The primary goal is to experimentally constrain potential violations of the Born rule, a fundamental postulate of quantum mechanics, using high-energy collider data.
main_result: The analysis sets an upper bound on the smearing parameter ($\epsilon$) due to Born-rule violations at $\epsilon < 0.042$ at 95% confidence level.
method: The authors model potential violations as a Gaussian angular smearing of the differential scattering cross section for Bhabha scattering, fitting this smeared prediction against existing experimental data.
model_or_system: The study focuses on large-angle Bhabha ($e^+e^- 	o e^+e^-$) scattering at $\sqrt{s}=29$ GeV, using data from the PEP collider. The deviation is parameterized by a smearing width $\epsilon$.
key_observables: Differential scattering cross section ($ rac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}$) as a function of $x = \cos	heta$.
important_parameters: The upper bound on the smearing parameter, $\epsilon < 0.042$; the center-of-mass energy $\sqrt{s}=29$ GeV; and the intrinsic experimental bin width $\Delta x = 0.05$.
main_assumptions: The constraint is model-independent, assuming that any deviation from the Born rule manifests as an angular smearing described by a Gaussian function.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares measured Bhabha scattering data against the standard QED prediction. Figure 2 shows the $\Delta\chi^2$ scan used to determine confidence limits on the smearing parameter $\epsilon$.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the theoretical motivation for testing the Born rule, details the phenomenological method using Gaussian smearing applied to Bhabha scattering cross sections, presents the statistical fitting procedure (likelihood/chi-squared minimization), and concludes with the derived upper bound on $\epsilon$.
why_interesting: While not directly focused on AMO systems, this work tests fundamental principles of quantum mechanics (the Born rule) using high-energy particle collision data, which is a core area of theoretical physics relevant to understanding measurement processes.
